UPSTREAM: cpufreq: mediatek: allow building as a module The MT8173 cpufreq driver can currently only be built-in, but it has a Kconfig dependency on the thermal core. THERMAL can be a loadable module, which in turn makes this driver impossible to build. It is nicer to make the cpufreq driver a module as well, so this patch turns the option in to a 'tristate' and adapts the dependency accordingly. The driver has no module_exit() function, so it will continue to not support unloading, but it can be built as a module and loaded at runtime now. UPSTREAM: thermal: Add Mediatek thermal controller support This adds support for the Mediatek thermal controller found on MT8173 and likely other SoCs. The controller is a bit special. UPSTREAM: iommu/io-pgtable-arm: Avoid dereferencing bogus PTEs In the case of corrupted page tables, or when an invalid size is given, __arm_lpae_unmap() may recurse beyond the maximum number of levels. Unfortunately the detection of this error condition only happens *after* calculating a nonsense offset from something which might not be a valid table pointer and dereferencing that to see if it is a valid PTE. Make things a little more robust by checking the level is valid before doing anything which depends on it being so. UPSTREAM: iommu/io-pgtable: Indicate granule for TLB maintenance IOMMU hardware with range-based TLB maintenance commands can work happily with the iova and size arguments passed via the tlb_add_flush callback, but for IOMMUs which require separate commands per entry in the range, it is not straightforward to infer the necessary granularity when it comes to issuing the actual commands. Add an additional argument indicating the granularity for the benefit of drivers needing to know, and update the ARM LPAE code appropriately (for non-leaf invalidations we currently just assume the worst-case page granularity rather than walking the table to check). UPSTREAM: iommu/arm-smmu: Invalidate TLBs properly When invalidating an IOVA range potentially spanning multiple pages, such as when removing an entire intermediate-level table, we currently only issue an invalidation for the first IOVA of that range. Since the architecture specifies that address-based TLB maintenance operations target a single entry, an SMMU could feasibly retain live entries for subsequent pages within that unmapped range, which is not good. Make sure we hit every possible entry by iterating over the whole range at the granularity provided by the pagetable implementation. UPSTREAM: iommu/io-pgtable: Add MTK 4GB mode in Short-descriptor In MT8173, Normally the first 1GB PA is for the HW SRAM and Regs, so the PA will be 33bits if the dram size is 4GB. We have a "DRAM 4GB mode" toggle bit for this. If it's enabled, from CPU's point of view, the dram PA will be from 0x1_00000000~0x1_ffffffff. In short descriptor, the pagetable descriptor is always 32bit. Mediatek extend bit9 in the lvl1 and lvl2 pgtable descriptor as the 4GB mode. In the 4GB mode, the bit9 must be set, then M4U help add 0x1_00000000 based on the PA in pagetable. Thus the M4U output address to EMI is always 33bits(the input address is still 32bits). We add a special quirk for this MTK-4GB mode. And in the standard spec, Bit9 in the lvl1 is "IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED", while it's AP[2] in the lvl2, therefore if this quirk is enabled, NO_PERMS is also expected. CHROMIUM: tpm-rng: Make hwrng working The patch fixes two issues to make hwrng working for ChromeOS. First, make sure that the tpm-tis module is initialized before tpm-rng. From the latency measurement listed below, it takes around 27ms for each rng_get_data call to TPM module to generate a 64-byte randomness on Ultima with Infineon TPM 1.2. The tpm-rng module makes a rng_get_data call in add_early_randomness in registration of hwrng which add a 27ms latency to the kernel boot time. Second, the quality of randomness of tpm-rng is set(default is off) in order to create additional kernel thread(named hwrng) to keep pumping data from TPM as one of the linux-rng sources for input_pool continuously. The value of the 'quality' is used for the ratio 'quality/1024', i.e. 1000/1024 here, of randomness bits generated by TPM to be added into the linux-rng entropy. For example, from the sequences of rng_get_data calls listed below, the rng_get_data calls in hwrng_fillfn function are in kthread hwrng which won't block the kernel boot up at all. The nonblocking pool got initialized after two fillups(add_early_randomness and the first rng_get_data call in hwrng_fillfn), then the hwrng kthread keeps filling up the input_pool until the entropy of input_pool is larger than 'random_write_wakeup_bits' or 896(28*32) bits(which is completed in another four rng_get_data calls in hwrng_fill). The seventh rng_get_data call(@2.081762) is triggered by borging ssl patch which makes the entropy got a bit lower by getrandom calls. In other words, if the available entropy drops to zero and no other rng sources available, tpm-rng should be able to fillup the entropy with four rng_get_data calls(1000 = 4 * (32 * 8 * 1000/1024) > The driver was not freeing the auxiliary batch buffer when we were setting the access domain for the PAK_OBJ command buffer. At the same time, the alignment was wrong and should have been at the cache line boundary. Finally, fix the order of operations for the pipline flush on SKL+.
